sentences.text: The holotype, which is the single specimen used to define the species, preserves an articulated right hindlimb containing the femur, fibula, tibia, and foot.
Measurements indicate the longest femur reached 247 mm, while the longest tibia measured 270 mm.
In this animal, the tibia is on average 13% longer than the femur, a proportion linked to cursorial habits.
Recent estimates suggest the creature had a total body length between 2 and 3 meters and a weight between 35 and 45 kg.

Aniksosaurus is distinguished by deep neural arches on cervical vertebrae, a wide neural canal, a ventral keel on caudal vertebrae, robust manual claws, narrow metatarsals and digit IV, an expanded brevis shelf on the ilium, and a deep notch on the femur.
The name means "spring lizard" because the fossils were found on September 21, the day spring begins in the Southern Hemisphere.
The species name darwini honors Charles Darwin, who visited Patagonia in 1832 and 1833.
The genus Aniksosaurus was established by Rubén Dario Martínez and Fernando Emilio Novas in 2006.
The type specimen was discovered at the Laguna Palacios Ranch locality in the Bajo Barreal Formation of Chubut, Argentina.
A 2013 study concluded that the holotype and four other individuals were juveniles to sub-adults based on histological analysis.
Histological analysis of two individuals suggested they were approximately three years old.
Monospecific bonebeds suggest Aniksosaurus was gregarious, providing a selective advantage over competitors.
It is probable that Aniksosaurus exhibited gregarious behavior only during a specific life stage, probably when it was a sub-adult.
Small scavengers likely fed on the animal, leaving tiny grooves on the femur after soft tissues decomposed.
No evidence of cannibalism or intraspecific competition was found in the fossil assemblage.
Martínez and Novas originally classified Aniksosaurus within the clade Coelurosauria based on hindlimb anatomy.
However, more recent research by Choiniere et al. found that Aniksosaurus is phylogenetically closer to members of the taxon Compsognathidae.
The parent group of Aniksosaurus is Compsognathidae.
Aniksosaurus lived during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages of the Cretaceous period, approximately 96 to 91 million years ago.

The Bajo Barreal Formation, where Aniksosaurus lived, also contained remains of Xenotarsosaurus, Drusilasaura, Epachthosaurus, Campylodoniscus, Secernosaurus, and teeth from carcharodontosaurids and dromaeosaurids.
Some sources state Aniksosaurus lived from the Cenomanian to the Turonian, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
